title: The Lock That Kept Its Word
logline: When a Hartsford herbalist hires Jory Brennick to haul his grandmother's locked chest out of a collapsing drowned house before new pilings seal its only entrance, the chest surfaces safely only for its lock to take the one payment the old rhyme promised: the family name spoken to open it.
promise: A race against a dock crew's building schedule through a collapsed drowned house, a lock that costs exactly what the old rhyme says it costs, and a water-stained remedy from before the Cataclysm that proves itself against a real fever in the present.
setting: the drowned streets below Hartsford and Shoreside, Sunken Reach, early autumn, about twenty years after the Cataclysm

cast.name: Jory Brennick
cast.want: to prove himself a salvager worth hiring on his own name, not just as Maud's son

cast.name: Maud Brennick
cast.want: to keep her son from underestimating the danger of the drowned streets she still remembers from before the flood
cast.appearance: auburn hair just starting to grey
cast.dress: short trousers, long sleeves, wide-brimmed hat

cast.name: Walter Ames
cast.station: Hartsford herbalist, descendant of the drowned town's apothecary family
cast.want: to recover his grandmother's sealed chest of remedies before the entrance is lost, hoping its cures can ease a fever moving through Hartsford
cast.appearance: A stooped man of sixty-one with a close white beard and ink-stained fingers from years of grinding herbs.
cast.dress: A patched wool coat over a leather apron, a brass magnifying loupe on a cord at his neck.
cast.voice_note: soft-spoken, apologizes before asking for anything

cast.name: Selah Vance
cast.station: Shoreside dock-builder, foreman of the stilt expansion crew
cast.want: to drive the new pilings and finish the stilt line before the first winter storm closes the harbor to construction
cast.appearance: A tall, broad-shouldered woman of thirty-eight with wind-cracked skin and dark hair cropped short under a canvas cap.
cast.dress: A heavy oiled coat and tall boots, a carpenter's plumb-line looped at her belt.
cast.voice_note: brisk, states facts rather than opinions

cast.name: Liora Quill
cast.want: to land a find notable enough that people stop calling her 'Jory's partner'
cast.appearance: A lean young woman of nineteen with a long braid of light brown hair, bleached pale at the tips by sun and salt.
cast.dress: A sleeveless diving vest over rolled trousers, a string of small brass fittings tied at her belt.

chapters.title: Six Days Before the Pilings
beats: Jory and Liora sort the morning's salvage on a Floatsome platform, trading friendly jabs about whose haul is better.
Walter Ames arrives by hired boat, asking the dockhands specifically for Jory by name.

Walter explains his grandmother's locked chest sits in a drowned house's cellar, that Shoreside's crew will drive new pilings through that exact street in six days, and that his family's claim to the flooded lot lapsed years ago, so he has no right to stop the work, only to beat it.
Maud, overhearing, warns that stretch lies close to the new fissure and hasn't been checked since a tremor loosened the harbor shelf.
Jory accepts the contract over Maud's objection, and she insists on coming along since her chart of that street is years out of date.

chapters.title: The Foreman's Schedule
beats: Jory, Liora, and Maud travel to Shoreside to confirm the timeline with foreman Selah Vance.
Selah states plainly her crew starts driving pilings into that street in six days and won't delay for a salvage job.
Selah adds that an early storm building off the coast could push her start forward, to five days or fewer.
Maud unrolls her old chart, marking the house, and admits she hasn't dived that stretch since the tremor.
At dawn they dive to the site and find the chart wrong: the entrance it marks is now buried under a fallen roof.

chapters.title: Through the Broken Window
beats: Jory and Liora find another way in, through a broken parlor window into the sunken room.
Inside, fresh chisel marks scar the wall near the strongbox, far too recent to be from the Cataclysm.
They find the strongbox bolted to a support beam, its bolts rusted but not fused, meaning it could be freed and raised rather than opened down here.
The lock itself has no keyhole, only raised letters shaped like a name, faintly warm through Jory's glove.
Running low on air, they surface, debating who else has already been down there before them.

chapters.title: A Name Spoken in Air
beats: Jory reports the chisel marks and the strange lock to Walter, who has no idea who could have gotten in before them.

Walter explains his grandmother sealed the box with material from the fissure, and that old lore holds the lock answers only to a voice speaking the household's true name three times in open air, never underwater.
Walter admits the old stories say the lock takes its own payment for the answer, though no one living has tested it.
Selah arrives to check progress and reveals her own survey crew chipped that same wall last week while marking piling positions, explaining the fresh marks.
Selah adds that the house sits directly under where one new piling is meant to go, meaning the box must be freed and raised within three days or be crushed in place.

chapters.title: What Maud Remembers
beats: Back at Floatsome, Jory relays the above-water rule and the lock's warmth to Maud.
Maud recalls, as a girl before the Cataclysm, children chanting a phrase for luck at that very threshold, naming the household three times.
She warns that a lock drawn from fissure material might ask more than the old rhyme admits, since nobody has tested one in twenty years.
Maud insists on coming to help haul the box clear, since freeing rusted bolts underwater is its own hazard.
A runner arrives from Shoreside: the storm has moved in faster than expected, and Selah's crew now starts driving pilings in two days, not three.

chapters.title: Raising the Box
beats: With two days left, Jory, Liora, and Maud dive together to the strongbox.
They work the corroded bolts loose with a pry bar, careful not to crack the beam and bring more of the roof down.
They rig a line and float the strongbox up through the broken window, breaking the surface at last.
Walter, waiting in the boat, takes the dripping box onto the deck, into open air, exactly as the rule requires.
Walter draws breath to begin the chant and notices the raised letters on the lock have smoothed away, as if waiting.

chapters.title: The Price
beats: Walter speaks the household's true name three times on the open deck, as Maud remembers it.
The lock answers, drawing a visible chill through his hand as it clicks open, his fingers going numb and pale.
Inside is not a ready chest of remedies but a water-stained formulary and a wrapped bundle of unfamiliar mineral.
Trying afterward to repeat his family's true name aloud, Walter finds he no longer can; the lock has taken the name itself as payment.
Maud recognizes the wrapped mineral as raw fissure-glass, the very substance worked into the lock, meaning the formulary's remedies were tested against it generations ago.

chapters.title: What the Chest Was For
beats: Onshore, they read the formulary together, Jory sounding out water-smudged passages describing a fever draught measured against that same mineral.
Walter decides to carry the formulary and the bundle straight to a Hartsford healer rather than test it himself, since the measures must be exact and the mineral is dangerous to mishandle.
Three days later, word returns that the healer's draught, matched to the old measures, has eased the fever moving through Hartsford.
Selah's crew drives the first pilings into the cleared street exactly on schedule, the house and its chest already clear of harm.

Walter pays Jory's contract in full and gives Maud a share for her memory of the chant, and Jory and Liora start eyeing the fissure itself as their next contract, with Maud cautiously agreeing to chart the way first this time.

notes: let's look at jory in the sunken reach with either someone contracting him to find something and he discovering  a mystery.
